markets.whyForex1Body: The largest market in the world trades 24 hours a day, five days a week, so majors stay liquid through every session.
markets.whyForex2Body: EUR/USD, GBP/USD and the other majors trade from 0.0 pips on Raw accounts, with fast MT5 execution.
markets.whyForex3Body: Size positions with flexible leverage up to 1:500, with margin shown live before you commit.
markets.faqForexQ1: What hours can I trade forex?
markets.faqForexA1: Forex runs 24 hours a day from Monday morning in Sydney to Friday evening in New York.
markets.faqForexQ2: What leverage is available on forex?
markets.faqForexA2: Leverage runs up to 1:500 on major pairs, subject to your account type and jurisdiction.
markets.faqForexQ3: What is the smallest trade size?
markets.faqForexA3: You can trade from 0.01 lots, so position sizing stays flexible for any account.
markets.faqForexA4: Positions held overnight carry a swap charge or credit, published live in the platform.
markets.whyIndices1Title: A whole market in one ticker
markets.whyIndices1Body: Trade the direction of the US 500, US 30 or major global indices without picking individual stocks.
markets.whyIndices2Body: Index CFDs track the underlying benchmark closely, with clear cash and futures pricing.
markets.whyIndices3Body: Go long or short on the same index to trade rallies and pullbacks alike.
markets.faqIndicesA1: You can trade major global benchmarks including US, European and Asian index CFDs.
markets.faqIndicesA2: Trading hours follow the exchange session of each index, with extended CFD hours where available.
markets.faqIndicesA3: Yes. Index CFDs let you open sell positions to trade falling markets.
markets.faqIndicesA4: Index CFD positions receive a dividend adjustment when constituents go ex-dividend.
markets.whyCommodities1Title: Gold and oil as macro hedges
markets.whyCommodities1Body: Commodities often move on inflation, rates and geopolitics, giving your book a hedge against equity swings.
markets.whyCommodities2Body: Gold and silver trade with tight pricing and, for partners, the deepest per-lot rebates.
markets.whyCommodities3Body: Oil and natural gas produce strong, tradable trends around supply and demand shifts.
markets.faqCommoditiesA1: Gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas and other major commodity CFDs are available.
markets.faqCommoditiesA2: Gold trades as XAU/USD, priced per ounce against the US dollar.
markets.faqCommoditiesA3: Yes. Commodity CFDs are margined, so leverage and margin are shown before you trade.
markets.faqCommoditiesA4: Spot metals and energies trade continuously, while dated contracts roll on schedule.
markets.whyStocks1Body: Take positions on Apple, Tesla, Amazon and hundreds of other global shares as CFDs.
markets.whyStocks2Body: Share CFDs track the stock price without you holding the underlying shares.
markets.whyStocks3Body: Trade rising and falling shares with clear margin requirements shown up front.
markets.faqStocksA1: Hundreds of US and international shares are available as CFDs.
markets.faqStocksA2: No. A share CFD tracks the price, so you never take custody of the stock.
markets.faqStocksA3: Yes. Share CFDs let you open sell positions to trade a falling stock.
markets.faqStocksQ4: Are dividends paid on stock CFDs?
markets.faqStocksA4: Open positions receive a dividend adjustment when the underlying goes ex-dividend.
markets.whyCrypto1Body: Bitcoin, Ethereum and major altcoins trade 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
markets.whyCrypto2Body: Crypto CFDs track the coin price, so there is no wallet to secure or exchange to fund.
markets.whyCrypto3Body: Trade both directions on the sharp moves of the market, with margin shown live.
markets.faqCryptoA1: Bitcoin, Ethereum and a range of major altcoins are available as CFDs.
markets.faqCryptoA2: Yes. Crypto CFDs trade around the clock, including weekends.
markets.faqCryptoQ3: Do I need a crypto wallet?
markets.faqCryptoA3: No. You trade the price movement, so no wallet or coin custody is required.
markets.faqCryptoA4: Yes. Crypto CFDs let you open sell positions to trade a falling market.
markets.whyEtfs1Body: An ETF CFD gives you exposure to a whole basket of assets through one instrument.
markets.whyEtfs2Body: Trade broad markets or specific sectors without buying each holding individually.
markets.whyEtfs3Body: Take a view in either direction on the ETF with clear, live margin.
markets.faqEtfsA1: It is a contract that tracks the price of an exchange-traded fund without owning it.
markets.faqEtfsA2: Major broad-market and sector ETFs are available as CFDs.
markets.faqEtfsA3: Yes. ETF CFDs let you open sell positions to trade a falling basket.
markets.faqEtfsA4: Positions receive a dividend adjustment when the underlying fund distributes.

tools.heroSubtitle: Margin, pip value, swap, pre-trade math without the spreadsheet.
tools.calcMarginDesc: The margin is the amount of capital required to open and maintain your position. It scales linearly with position size and inversely with leverage.
tools.calcPipFormula: Pip value = Lot size × Pip size × Contract size
tools.calcPipDesc: Each pip movement on your position is worth this amount. Multiply by your expected pip gain/loss to estimate P&L.
tools.calcSwapFormula: Swap = Swap rate × Lot size × Days
tools.calcSwapDesc: Swap is charged daily for holding positions overnight. Wednesday swap is tripled to account for the weekend.

pivot.heroSubtitle: Compute Classical, Camarilla, Woodie or Fibonacci pivots from yesterday's high, low and close, ready for today's session.
pivot.formulaClassicalDesc: The benchmark for intraday support and resistance. R and S levels fan out symmetrically around P using the prior session range.
pivot.formulaCamarillaDesc: Camarilla anchors on the close. Price tends to revert to the centre, while a break of R3 or S3 signals momentum.
pivot.formulaWoodieDesc: Woodie weights the close twice, pulling the pivot toward where the session ended.
pivot.formulaFibDesc: Golden ratio retracements (38.2%, 61.8%, 100%) applied to the session range to flag likely turning points.
